        **Title**: Fully_dynamic_biconnectivity_in_tildemathcalOlog2_n_time_77eacc0e2832a91d
        **Abstract**: We present a deterministic fully-dynamic data structure for maintaining information about
the cut-vertices in a graph; i.e. the vertices whose removal would disconnect the graph. Our
data structure supports insertion and deletion of edges, as well as queries to whether a pair
of connected vertices are either biconnected, or can be separated by a cutvertex, and in the
latter case we support access to separating cutvertices. All update operations are supported in
amortized O(log2 n log2 log n) time, and queries take worst-case O(log n log2 log n) time. Note
that these time bounds match the current best for deterministic dynamic connectivity up to
log log n factors.
The previous best algorithm for biconnectivity had an update time of O(log4 n log log n) by
Thorup [STOC’00], based on the O(log5 n) algorithm by Holm, de Lichtenberg, and Thorup
[STOC’98].
We obtain our improved running time by a series of reductions from the original problem
into well-defined data structure problems. While we do indeed apply the well-known techniques
for improving running time of two-edge connectivity [STOC’00, SODA’18], surprisingly, these
techniques alone do not lead to an update time of ˜O(log3 n), let alone the ˜O(log2 n) we give as a
final result.
Our contributions include a formally defined transient expose operation, which can be thought
of as a cheaper read-only expose operation on a top tree. For each vertex in the graph, we
maintain a data structure over its neighbors, and in this data structure we apply biasing (twice)
to save an ˜O(log n) factor (twice, so two ˜O(log n) factors). One of these biasing techniques is a
new, simple biased disjoint sets data structure, which may be of independent interest. Moreover,
in this neighborhood data structure, we facilitate that the vertex can select two VIP neighbors
that get special treatment, corresponding to its potentially two neighbors on an exposed path,
improving an otherwise log n-time operation down to constant time. It is this combination of
VIP neighbors with the transient expose operation that saves an ˜O(log n)-factor from another
bottle neck.

**Core Innovation:**
The paper presents a deterministic, fully dynamic data structure that efficiently maintains biconnectivity information in a graph, supporting edge insertions, deletions, and queries about cut vertices with improved time complexities.

**Technical Approach:**
1. **Top Tree Data Structure:** Utilizes top trees to represent the graph's biconnected components, enabling efficient hierarchical decomposition.
2. **Transient Expose Operation:** Introduces a cheaper read-only expose operation that facilitates quick access to necessary information without modifying the data structure.
3. **Biased Disjoint Sets:** Employs a new biased disjoint sets data structure that reduces time complexity by a log n factor, applied twice to achieve further optimizations.
4. **VIP Neighbors:** Implements a mechanism to identify and utilize "VIP" neighbors, allowing certain operations to run in constant time by leveraging exposed paths.

- **Update Operations:** Amortized time complexity of O(log²n log log n).
- **Queries:** Worst-case time complexity of O(log n log² log n).

**Limitations & Assumptions:**

**Domain Impact:**
- **Theoretical:** Advances graph theory by improving dynamic biconnectivity algorithms.
- **Practical:** Enhances network analysis in fields like network reliability, social networks, and computational biology, offering real-time applications and efficient query handling.

- The time complexities are critical: O(log²n log log n) for updates and O(log n log² log n) for queries, demonstrating significant efficiency improvements over previous methods.
